findings.lines: transferAndCall: 'mem[64] = ceil32(data.length) + 160 / mem[160 len data.length] = data[all]' ... 'log Transfer(..., uint256 value=mem[mem[64] len ceil32(data.length) - mem[64] + 192])'; the ERC677 Transfer log and the tokenFallback call below it
findings.decompiled: mem[ceil32(data.length) + 160] = value / log Transfer(address indexed from=caller, address indexed to=address(to), uint256 value=mem[mem[64] len ceil32(data.length) - mem[64] + 192])  |  log Transfer(address from, address to, uint256 value, bytes data): mem[mem[64] len _36 - mem[64]], ...  |  call address(to) with: args mem[mem[64] len _45 - mem[64]]
findings.source: RIFToken.sol:279-285 transfer(_to, _value) (emit Transfer(msg.sender, _to, _value)); emit Transfer(msg.sender, _to, _value, _data); receiver.tokenFallback(msg.sender, _value, _data)
findings.issue: In every other function the Transfer value prints as the variable, but here, after the bytes argument is copied to memory and the free pointer set to ceil32(data.length) + 160, mem[64] is not forwarded: the value is a memory range, the ERC677 event's data and the tokenFallback(address,uint256,bytes) call (0xc0ee0b8a) stay raw memory. Only constant addresses 0 and 32 are written between the store to mem[64] and these reads.
findings.rule: A copy to mem[a len n] with a constant a >= 96 cannot touch [64, 96) for any n (memory sizes are below 2^64, so a + n does not wrap); with that, forward mem[64] = ceil32(data.length) + 160 to the later reads, and the log's range reduces to the word 'value' (and the call to tokenFallback(caller, value, data)).

notes: solc 0.4.26. No source loops; the four whiles are the compiler's word-by-word copies of the bytes argument into the event data and the call buffer (two per bytes-taking function, P7), each followed by the 0.4-style tail masking ('~(256**(32 - n % 32) - 1) & mem[...]'). Reviewed: transfer / transferFrom / approve / increase/decrease allowance, the distribution-time and redeem checks, the minimum-balance tracking (stor6) after transfers, transferAndCall; the remaining getters and admin functions checked. P8: the mem[0]/mem[32] hash scratch writes kept before mapping reads.
summary: Faithful; the only notable defect is that in the bytes-taking transfers the free pointer is not forwarded past the bytes copy, leaving the Transfer value, the ERC677 event and the tokenFallback call as raw memory.
